question: Cheraw, the bamboo dance performed using crossed bamboo sticks, is a folk dance of which state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cheraw**, also known as the **bamboo dance**, is one of the most famous traditional dances of **Mizoram**.
 
• The dance involves the use of **long bamboo sticks**, which are held horizontally and tapped rhythmically on the ground by performers.
 
• The performers (usually women) move gracefully in and out of the bamboo sticks to the beat of the music without getting their feet caught.
 
• This dance holds **cultural and religious significance** for the Mizo community, as it is often performed during **festivals and special occasions**, such as weddings or harvest celebrations.
 
• The Cheraw dance reflects the **rich heritage and traditions** of the state of Mizoram.
 
• It symbolizes the **harmony and coordination** between nature and mankind through its intricate movements.
 
• Cheraw has gained international fame and is considered a **symbol of Mizoram's cultural identity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Meghalaya**__

 __
 
• Meghalaya is known for its **rich tribal culture** and several traditional dances, such as **Wangala Dance**, performed by the Garo tribe to celebrate the harvest festival.
 
• Another famous dance is the **Shad Suk Mynsiem**, performed by the Khasi tribe during the spring season.
 
 
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh**__
 __
 
• Arunachal Pradesh is famous for its diverse tribal dances such as **Yak Dance, Buiya Dance, and Ajilamu Dance**.
 
• These dances are often linked to **religious rituals** and **seasonal celebrations**.
 
 
 
• **Sikkim**__
 
 
• Sikkim is known for its traditional dances like the **Chu-Faat Dance** and **Mask Dance**, performed during religious festivals.
 
• These dances are deeply rooted in **Buddhist culture** and depict various mythological stories and traditions.
